about: How fast one sending inbox may send, and what each bounce, reply or complaint means, as DATA. A pacing row is a ramp (how many sends a day, by the inbox's day number since its first send), the least gap between sends, the weekdays and local hours a send may go, how long to leave an address after it was sent to, and when to pause the whole inbox (a share of bounces or any complaint over the last sends). An outcome row says when it applies (every condition on a field of a normalised event must hold: equals one of the values, contains one of the words, or matches the pattern) and what it means (kind) and asks (action, one of the actions below). Event fields come from the event-sources rows, so a new provider is a new row. The first outcome row that applies wins. The actions are listed strongest first: when one address has several outcomes (a reply, then an out-of-office), the strongest action holds, so a later, weaker event never undoes a bounce, a complaint or a reply. Every number, word and weekday is a knob; a person's own rows replace these through pacing_row, outcome_rows and event_source_row.
